hints: Focus on the two functional groups in the same molecule, an alcohol and a carboxylic acid, and what concentrated sulfuric acid encourages them to do.
Count the atoms that will join the new ring, the O from CH2(OH) plus the four carbons of CH2-CH=CH-C=O gives a 5-membered lactone with water lost.
Check where the C=C stays and which end bonds to O, the O must stay on the CH2 end and the C=O must stay on the CH end to make an ester link.
walkthrough:
**Spot the hydroxy acid**

You have HO-CH2-CH=CH-COOH in one molecule. That is both an alcohol on the left and a carboxylic acid on the right.

Starting material:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$$

**Recall intramolecular esterification**

An alcohol plus a carboxylic acid forms an ester plus water. Here it happens inside the same molecule, so it makes a cyclic ester called a lactone.

General rule:
$$\text{R-OH + HOOC-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-OOC-R' + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Build the ring size and keep the double bond**

Join the alcoholic O to the carboxylic C=O carbon. The ring contains O + CH2 + CH + CH + C=O, which is 5 atoms, a gamma-lactone. Warm dilute acid does not destroy the C=C, so it stays in the ring.

Reaction:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH=CHCOOH} \rightarrow \text{cyclic O-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-C(=O)- + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Pick the correct skeletal orientation**

The ester link must be O-C(=O). So O is bonded to CH2 and to C=O, while C=O is bonded to O and to CH of the double bond. That is O-CH2-CH=CH-C(=O) around the ring, which matches only one skeletal drawing.

options.A: Incorrect. The O is not bonded to the C=O carbon, so this is not an ester. It looks like a cyclic enol ether with a separate ketone, which cannot form from simple loss of water between OH and CO2H.
options.B: Incorrect. Although this has an ester O-C=O link, the O is attached to the C=C end instead of the CH2 end. That reverses the chain and would require the OH to have been on the alkene carbon, which it was not.
options.C: Correct. This is the 5-membered unsaturated lactone O-CH2-CH=CH-C(=O). The O bonds to CH2 and to C=O, the C=O bonds to O and to CH, and the C=C is retained, exactly what intramolecular esterification of HOCH2CH=CHCOOH gives plus H2O.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows two C=O groups in the ring, a cyclic anhydride type structure. Our starting material has only one CO2H group and loses only one H2O, so a second C=O cannot appear.
